**We have 1,600 customers.**

I counted them in the customer master table (`sahil-devx.dev_dna_silver.customers_master`), which holds one row per customer, deduplicated across all sales channels. The semantic layer has no "customer count" measure for this table, so I counted with a direct SQL query.

The table has no duplicate or removed records, so every way of counting gives 1,600:

| Check | Value |
|---|---|
| Total rows | 1,600 |
| Distinct `customer_master_id` | 1,600 |
| Rows marked as the current version (`rn = 1`) | 1,600 |
| Rows flagged as deleted (`is_deleted`) | 0 |
| Rows with no customer ID | 0 |

This counts everyone with a customer record, not just people who ordered recently. I can split it by acquisition channel, country or loyalty tier, or count only customers who ordered in a given period.
